alerts.title: Windows Security log cleared
alerts.description: Event 1102: the Security audit log was cleared. This is rarely legitimate and is classic anti-forensics. Preserve whatever logs remain (forwarded copies, other hosts) and find out who did it.

alerts.title: Root shell opened through sudo
alerts.description: sudo used to start an interactive root shell (bash, sh, su -, ...). Legitimate admins do this, but it bypasses per-command sudo logging, so it is worth a look.

alerts.title: sudo denied (user not allowed or wrong password)
alerts.description: A user tried sudo and was refused. One-offs are usually mistakes; repeats, or service accounts like www-data trying sudo, suggest someone probing for privilege escalation.

alerts.title: File deleted from PowerShell
alerts.description: A file was deleted through PowerShell (Remove-Item / del / rm / erase). Usually routine; important when the file name or the account is sensitive, or when it lines up with other alerts (indicator removal).
